h1: Arbor presses, bench presses, turret punch presses and orbital riveters
intro: Hand presses for the tool room, the maintenance shop and the sheet-metal shop: arbor presses from 1/2 to 8 tons for pressing bearings, bushings and pins, broaching keyways and staking; ratchet and rack-and-pinion presses for repeated small-part work; bench presses that punch, flare, bead, louver, notch and bend sheet with standard tooling; manual turret punch presses with twelve punches on the turret; and orbital riveting machines that form solid rivets without hammering. NovoTech's value-line presses are built in China to our specification, with parts and tooling from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What size arbor press do I need?
faq.a: Choose by the force and the size of the part. A 1 – 2 ton press handles small bearings, pins and staking; 3 – 5 tons most automotive and machine bearings and broaching; 6 – 8 tons larger bearings and gears, with up to 17.7″ of height and 10″ of diameter between the ram and the base. For more force, see the hydraulic shop presses.

faq.q: What can the bench press do in the HVAC and sheet-metal shop?
faq.a: With the standard tooling: punch round, square and oblong holes, punch and flare or punch and bead holes for stiffness and hoses, cut louvers 1 – 5″ long, notch corners, bend 90° in 3/8″ mild steel and shear 16 ga. The EBP-10T is the hydraulic version for heavier and repeated work; the BP3-F holds four tools at once for production.

The riveting head is tilted a few degrees and rolls around the rivet end, forming the head gradually with about a tenth of the force a punch would need. The part does not deform, the head is smooth and the machine is quiet — used for hinges, chain links, brake parts, appliances and hardware. With other tools the XM riveters work as normal presses.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
